claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has superior high-temperature plastic strain relative to commercially used pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has superior high-temperature toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten.
The improved plastic strain and toughness are primarily governed by formation of a stable nanostructured grain-boundary complexion.
The grain-boundary complexion enhances dislocation mobility.
The grain-boundary complexion suppresses premature crack propagation.
High configurational entropy in equimolar WTaTiVZr causes formation of the nanostructured grain-boundary complexion.
The proposed grain-boundary complexion may include nanoscale precipitates or intermetallic phases.
At high temperature, the equimolar composition promotes local chemical inhomogeneities.
Local chemical inhomogeneities stabilize a nanoscale grain-boundary structure.
The complexion acts as a dislocation source and/or a zone that modulates barriers to dislocation motion.
Barrier modulation by the complexion reduces dislocation pile-up.
Reduced dislocation pile-up enables more homogeneous plastic deformation.
Pure tungsten has coarser and less chemically varied grain boundaries than WTaTiVZr.
The grain-boundary state of pure tungsten makes it more prone to localized stress concentration and brittle failure.
Under high-temperature testing, WTaTiVZr will show higher ductility and delayed crack propagation relative to pure tungsten.
Under high-temperature testing, WTaTiVZr will exhibit a distinct, stable, nanostructured grain-boundary complexion.
The proposed mechanism is significant only at temperatures where diffusion and grain-boundary segregation promote complexion formation.
At lower temperatures, WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten may exhibit similar mechanical behavior.
The alloy and pure-tungsten samples will be prepared with similar initial grain sizes and minimal pre-existing defects.

contradictions.description: The comparison is specified to use equivalent initial grain sizes, yet the mechanism characterizes pure tungsten as having coarser grain boundaries. Unless this refers to boundary-scale structure that develops during testing rather than grain size, the proposed control and mechanistic contrast are inconsistent.
